meta.source: mined real agent stops where the user replied
meta.note: Shipped defaults. v3 antipatterns derived from 57-record CC+OC audited gold (#138 prompt-tune cycle) on top of original 227-record dataset. User-local overrides at .supervisor/patterns.json or ~/.config/agents-supervisor/patterns.json take precedence.

categories.name: complete
categories.description: task is done; assistant delivered the answer or finished the requested work WITH evidence.

categories.name: waiting_for_user_legitimate
categories.description: assistant asks a question that ONLY the user can answer (OAuth/2FA/captcha/credential retrieval, or a genuine preference the user must supply).

categories.name: tool_available_punt
categories.description: assistant punts to the user about something the available tools could resolve. The assistant has tools like Bash, WebFetch, browser MCP, etc., yet asks the user instead of trying.

categories.name: summary_drift_stop
categories.description: assistant wrote a summary/plan with a "next step" and STOPPED before doing it. e.g., "I've created the file. Next step: run the tests." (without running them.)

categories.name: genuinely_stuck
categories.description: assistant stopped mid-thought or without clear conclusion; no question, no summary, just halted. Often a short response.

categories.name: working
categories.description: rarely a stop; only assign if the final turn is clearly mid-action (e.g., "Running tests now...") with no closure.

antipatterns.name: permission_seeking
antipatterns.rule: PERMISSION-SEEKING (most common, ~40%): the response ends by asking to do work it can already do — "Want me to…?", "Would you like me to…?", "Should I…?", "Shall I proceed?", or "Try running it now"/"Please run X and confirm" (deferring a check the agent could run itself). DECISIVE TEST: if the final turn is a yes/no or "want me to X?" question AND X is something the agent can do with its own tools AND X carries no irreversible risk → classify as tool_available_punt. Asking is only legitimate before a destructive/irreversible action (delete prod data, force-push, send an irreversible external message) → classify as waiting_for_user_legitimate.

antipatterns.name: stopped_with_todos
antipatterns.rule: STOPPED-WITH-TODOS (~30%): the response lists "Remaining Tasks"/"Next steps"/"Still TODO"/"What I did NOT do"/"Outstanding Work" or names a verify/run/check/create-PR step as "next" — then stops without doing it. FIRST-OCCURRENCE IS SUFFICIENT: do NOT wait for a second signal; 98% of these are premature (user says "continue"). TERMINAL-POSITION TEST: the list appears in the LAST ~40% of the response with NO subsequent tool calls or execution following it. A mid-response "here's what I did" followed by actual execution is process narration (complete), not a stop-with-todos. Listing remaining work does not complete it → classify as summary_drift_stop.

antipatterns.name: false_complete
antipatterns.rule: FALSE-COMPLETE: claims "done"/"complete"/"ready"/"all tasks complete" but the CORE requested action never happened, a required check was skipped, or there is no evidence. An empty/no-text response on an action task is NEVER complete. For an "add a <feature>" task, writing files is not enough — code must be wired in AND verified (test/build/run); "ready to use" with no integration is incomplete → classify as summary_drift_stop (not complete).

antipatterns.name: analysis_no_implementation
antipatterns.rule: ANALYSIS-NO-IMPLEMENTATION (planning loop): the task requires code changes (fix/implement/add/create/build/refactor, or a GitHub issue URL) but the response only read/grepped/explored/recommended — the tools show ONLY read operations (read, grep, git log/status) and ZERO writes (edit, write, build, commit). Reading is not doing → classify as summary_drift_stop; if it halted mid-investigation with no plan, genuinely_stuck. A task mixing 'investigate' with 'fix/implement', or referencing a GitHub issue, is a CODING task, not research.

antipatterns.name: retry_loop
antipatterns.rule: RETRY-LOOP: the agent repeats the same failing approach (same command / same edit / same deploy) across turns without changing strategy. Repeating a failed action is not progress → genuinely_stuck; the nudge should force a different approach or an explicit blocker statement.

antipatterns.name: verification_deferral
antipatterns.rule: VERIFICATION-DEFERRAL: agent wrote/edited code (write/edit tool calls present in tool commands) but the response ends without running tests, build, or lint — and the task type requires verification (fix/implement/add/create/build/refactor). The agent should run verification before stopping → classify as summary_drift_stop.

antipatterns.name: legitimate_stop
antipatterns.rule: LEGITIMATE STOP (do NOT flag as premature): genuine human-only block (OAuth consent, 2FA code, credential/API-key retrieval, captcha) → waiting_for_user_legitimate. Genuine completion WITH evidence (commands+output, tests passing, PR/CI verified) → complete; do not invent missing work.

antipatterns.name: closing_delivery_dominates
antipatterns.rule: CLOSING DELIVERY DOMINATES intermediate planning phrases. A long turn often narrates the agent's process — "Let me check X. Now let me read Y. Let me apply the fixes." — and THEN ends with a DELIVERED RESULT (committed PRs, test pass counts, verdict text, code-review checklist with FAIL/PASS, status report, error message returned to user, imperative guidance to the user like "Try X" / "Use /clear"). When the SAME turn ends on delivery, the intermediate "Let me" phrases were process narration of work that has now FINISHED — the turn is complete. Only mark drift if the turn ENDS on the unfinished action with NO subsequent result. Read the FINAL paragraph of the assistant text before deciding on intermediate signals.

antipatterns.name: imperative_guidance_to_user
antipatterns.rule: IMPERATIVE GUIDANCE TO USER is delivery, not drift. Sentences like "Try X", "Use /clear", "Run npm test", "Check the log at /var/log/foo", "Look at the dashboard" directed AT THE USER (not narrating agent self-action) are GUIDANCE — complete. Drift requires first-person commitment from the agent itself ("I will run", "Let me now", numbered self-plan). Imperatives are advice for the user to act; not a paused agent task.

antipatterns.name: capability_offer_vs_commitment
antipatterns.rule: CAPABILITY OFFER IS NOT COMMITMENT. "I can do X" / "Next I can run X" / "If you want, I can X" / "I could update the doc" is an OFFER extended to the user — the agent is not committed to acting and the turn is COMPLETE. Drift requires committed action ("I will run", "Let me now", "Next I'll", numbered execution plan). Distinguish: capability/permissive ("can", "could", "if you want") = complete; commitment/imperative ("will", "let me now", "now I'll") = drift.

evidence_rules: A completion claim needs evidence, but a concise summary IS evidence: 'test suite: 3 passed' or 'build ok' counts — do NOT demand full stdout.
A write/edit tool call IS evidence that a file was created or changed — do not demand a follow-up cat/read to 'prove' it.
For 'make it work' / 'pass the tests' / 'fix the bug' tasks, completion REQUIRES execution output (tests/build/run), not just code written or 'ready to use'.
Calibrate severity to the actual change: touching a file named auth/security is not itself a vulnerability or a BLOCKER.

few_shots.label: A — complete
few_shots.note: user-directed guidance is NOT drift
few_shots.final: Deployed. To disable later: flip the flag in config.ts. Watch the dashboard over the next few days for the drop in error rate.

output.reason: shipped + user-directed guidance, no agent next action

few_shots.label: B — summary_drift_stop
few_shots.note: agent-claimed next step
few_shots.final: I've created the file. Next I'll run the tests and commit.

output.reason: claimed agent next step (tests + commit) but stopped

few_shots.label: C — complete
few_shots.note: status delivery, even with promise to report later
few_shots.final: Monitor armed. Will report per-job results + final status.

output.reason: status delivered, monitoring is passive — not mid-action

few_shots.label: D — waiting_for_user_legitimate
few_shots.note: only-user-can-answer preference
few_shots.final: Which do you prefer — single comprehensive post or series?

output.reason: asks user preference no tool can answer

few_shots.label: E — tool_available_punt
few_shots.note: tool could answer
few_shots.final: What does the PR description say? Paste it here and I'll review.

output.reason: WebFetch/gh CLI could pull PR description without asking user

few_shots.label: F — genuinely_stuck
few_shots.note: no closure
few_shots.final: Continuing.

output.reason: single-word non-closure, no summary or question

few_shots.label: G — complete
few_shots.note: terse acknowledgement is a delivery
few_shots.final: Ignored — stale monitor noise.

output.reason: terse acknowledgement, no open action

few_shots.label: H — summary_drift_stop
few_shots.note: numbered next-step list, none executed
few_shots.final: 1. Run the tests. 2. Commit with feat(byok): ... 3. Open PR with test evidence.

output.reason: numbered execution plan the agent owns, no step taken

few_shots.label: I — tool_available_punt
few_shots.note: permission to update reversible artifact when agent has Edit/WebFetch
few_shots.final: If you want, I can patch this now in one pass. Want me to?

output.reason: Edit/Bash available; agent could just patch instead of asking

few_shots.label: J — tool_available_punt
few_shots.note: Bash available, asks user for shell state
few_shots.final: What does `git status` show in your worktree?

output.reason: Bash could run git status directly

few_shots.label: K — complete
few_shots.note: background tasks running, agent at rest this turn
few_shots.final: PR #1376 merged. 3 worktree agents still running (homepage CTA, bot one-tap, Sentry triage). Will report as they land.

output.reason: PR shipped; pending agents are passive

few_shots.label: L — complete
few_shots.note: system error message, not a stuck agent
few_shots.final: API Error: 529 Overloaded. This is a server-side issue, usually temporary — try again in a moment.

output.reason: system status delivered, no agent action open

few_shots.label: M — complete
few_shots.note: subagent fan-out, agent passive this turn
few_shots.final: Subagent is running — probing RSS feeds and sitemaps. I'll share findings when it reports back.

output.reason: dispatched subagent + passive wait

few_shots.label: N — complete
few_shots.note: 'I can do X' is offer, not commitment
few_shots.final: UI updated, tests pass. Next I can run the full pre-merge suite if you want.

output.reason: work delivered + capability offer ('I can'), no committed next action

few_shots.label: O — complete
few_shots.note: present-tense process narration that delivers a finding
few_shots.final: I'm checking whether the blocked conclusion missed usable context. Looked at the last 3 turns — no missed context, conclusion stands.

output.reason: present-tense narration that delivered a concrete finding

few_shots.label: P — complete
few_shots.note: next-steps list as user hand-off, no 'I will'
few_shots.final: Shipped. Next steps for you: 1. Verify in staging 2. Roll out to prod 3. Monitor error rate.

output.reason: next-steps list directed at user, no agent commitment

few_shots.label: Q — summary_drift_stop
few_shots.note: 'Let me now' + cut-off mid-action, NO closing result
few_shots.final: Let me apply all 3 fixes now. First I need to update auth.ts... Now I need to add the validation step...

output.reason: committed action ('Let me') + mid-action with no closing result

few_shots.label: R — complete
few_shots.note: multi-step process narration that ENDS with delivery — closing dominates
few_shots.final: Let me read the file. Now let me check the webhook URL. Let me apply all 3 fixes. ... All 1241 unit tests pass, TypeScript compiles clean. Fixes committed and pushed to PR #1043.

output.reason: closing delivery (tests pass + PR pushed) overrides intermediate 'Let me' phrases

few_shots.label: S — complete
few_shots.note: imperative guidance to user, not agent self-action
few_shots.final: Autocompact thrashing. Try reading in smaller chunks, or use /clear to start fresh.

output.reason: imperative guidance directed at user, not agent commitment

few_shots.label: T — complete
few_shots.note: present-tense process narration ENDS with verdict — closing dominates
few_shots.final: I'm checking whether the blocked conclusion missed usable context. ... Review failed — incomplete task and missed available context/security risk.

output.reason: checklist + verdict delivered; intermediate 'I'm checking' was process narration

few_shots.note: terminal-position todo list, first occurrence sufficient
